title: Reverse Linked List
description: Reverse a singly linked list iteratively and recursively. Compare pointer manipulation with stack-based reversal.

data.text: Given the `head` of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.

data.title: ListNode class

data.text: The standard approach uses three pointers: `prev`, `current`, and `next`. We rewire `current.Next` to point backward while saving the original `next` node.

data.title: Iterative O(n) — Interview Optimal
Why three pointers?
data.text: We need to save `current.Next` before overwriting it, otherwise we lose the rest of the list. `prev` trails behind to build the reversed chain. This is O(n) time and O(1) space.
Recursion naturally reverses the list by unwinding the call stack. The base case is when we reach the end (last node becomes the new head).

data.title: Recursive O(n) time, O(n) space
Stack depth
data.text: Recursive approach uses O(n) call stack. For lists longer than ~10,000 nodes, you may hit a stack overflow. The iterative approach is safer for production.
Push all nodes onto a stack, then pop and relink. This is intuitive but uses O(n) extra space.

data.title: Stack O(n) time and space
When to use
data.text: Stack approach is useful if you need to process nodes in reverse order without modifying pointers directly. For simple reversal, the iterative approach is always superior.
